chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: Robichaux's library and trumpeters Kimball and Perez
summary: Tulane holds Robichaux's orchestrations; Garland recalls the early Robichaux lineup and compares Andrew Kimball and Manuel Perez as trumpeters.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We've got Robichaux's library, we've got 7,000 orchestrations of his. Yeah, we have?
Yeah, up at Tulane where I work.
Yeah? You ought to see them.
You got John's, huh? Yeah. I don't remember that band.
I don't know...
They're still using those things, they're still using Red Book. I don't know that band. When we first had that band, they had Henry Kimmel on the bass.
Mm-hmm.

He had Charlie McCurtis on the clarinet. Mm-hmm. He had Buddy Christian on the guitar. Walter Brundee on the drums. Mm-hmm. And John was on the violin. And Kimmel, not Andrew Kimmel, before Andrew Kimmel was a fellow that built. Jim Williams was playing trumpet. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. That's before Andrew, and Kimball came in.
Yeah, and Kimball was with him in the 20s, I believe. Late years.
Yeah, that was the band.

Yeah, I'm sure of that, because Alvin Alcorn told me that Kimball would play some of the Jolly Roll Morton numbers that got published, you know, from the orchestration, and he could really get hot. Which I never knew that Kimball was a hot man at all, I didn't know he was a get-off man.
Oh, Andrew?
Yeah.
Well, he wasn't too hot, he was pretty good.
Was he hotter than Manuel Perez?

I'm going to tell you that there you are, there's two good men, two good men you call in there, Manuel and Kimball. Both. I don't know, I don't know, there wasn't a mood. There wasn't too hot on the jazz, you know. They played, there was good trumpet players.
Good musician, good trumpet players. Oh my goodness.

Reed. Now you talk about Reed. Two guys. Really good Reed. They wind up to those two guys, man, they had the Excelsa band, the Onwards band. They wouldn't use nobody but he and Kimball on trumpet. They didn't use no three or four trumpets. They're seeing Andrew. They only used two trumpets and ten or twelve piece brass band. That would be alright, wouldn't it? It would be alright, but they had two strong men there, you know. Yeah.
Each man hold his own. Sometimes it's better that way, if you have two good men rather than three bad ones.
No, well them guys.
They play a nice harmony and everything.

Well you'll find that on Carnival Day, like Labor Day when they got all them bands out. You'll have to come out there with a horn and don't know what you're doing. You just got a horn holding up your mouth.
Mm-hmm.
